questions.stem: Why did Maharṣi Aṇīmāṇḍavya curse Yama-Dharma?
stem_variants: What was the reason behind Sage Aṇīmāṇḍavya placing a curse on Yama?
options: For misinterpreting and disproportionately executing Dharma
For refusing to let him enter heaven
For causing the death of his disciples
For failing to punish the king who impaled him
distractor_pool: For ignoring the theft in his hermitage
questions.answer: For misinterpreting and disproportionately executing Dharma
accepted_answers: For misinterpreting and disproportionately executing Dharma
questions.explanation: Aṇīmāṇḍavya lived on the spear and later cursed Yama-Dharma for misinterpreting Dharma by punishing a child's innocent actions disproportionately, demonstrating that even Dharmadeva is not above Dharma.
questions.source_quote: When he reached Yama's abode, he cursed Yama-Dharma for misinterpreting Dharma. Even Dharmadeva is not above Dharma.

questions.stem: According to the critique presented in the chapter, what fundamental flaw characterized Devavrata's vow?
stem_variants: Why does the text criticize Bhīṣma's renunciation and vow of celibacy?
options: It was taken without counsel and served only his father's personal desire (kāma) rather than state survival
It directly violated the explicit commands of the sage Vasiṣṭha
It was coerced by Satyavatī's father under threat of war
It prevented him from gaining the boon of choosing his time of death
distractor_pool: It caused the immediate death of King Śantanu
It led to the abandonment of the ancestral capital of Hastināpura
questions.answer: It was taken without counsel and served only his father's personal desire (kāma) rather than state survival
accepted_answers: It was taken without counsel and served only his father's personal desire (kāma) rather than state survival
questions.explanation: The text notes that neither the king's life nor the security of the realm was threatened; the vow was enacted without counsel to satisfy Śantanu's kāma, ultimately leaving the throne vulnerable and unstable.
questions.source_quote: The book questions it: his father's life, the kingdom and his own life did not depend on it; it only served his father's kāma.

questions.stem: How does the text evaluate Gāndhārī's decision to blindfold herself throughout her marital life?
stem_variants: What strategic and moral flaw is attributed to Gāndhārī's vow of lifelong blindfolding?
options: It was an emotional impulse that disabled her ability to perceive and correct Duryodhana's growing adharma
It was an act of explicit rebellion against the Kuru elders that divided the court
It breached the Vedic injunctions governing the duties of a kṣatriya queen
It was done solely to express contempt toward Bhīṣma for arranging the marriage
distractor_pool: It compelled Dhṛtarāṣṭra to abdicate the throne in favor of Pāṇḍu
It prevented her from participating in state sacrifices
questions.answer: It was an emotional impulse that disabled her ability to perceive and correct Duryodhana's growing adharma
accepted_answers: It was an emotional impulse that disabled her ability to perceive and correct Duryodhana's growing adharma
questions.explanation: Rather than being her blind husband's vision and guiding her sons, Gāndhārī's hasty vow resulted in turning a blind eye to Duryodhana's ego and misconduct, failing the true role of maternal influence.
questions.source_quote: The hasty vow blinded her to Duryodhana's stubbornness and ego... Had she instead been her husband's eyes, things might differ.

questions.stem: In what crucial manner did Bhīma's relationship with his vows differ from that of Bhīṣma or Arjuna?
stem_variants: Why does the text argue that Bhīma's vows did not cloud his judgment during the conflict?
options: He remained open to abandoning his vows for peace during diplomatic consultations and struck Duryodhana upon Kṛṣṇa's tactical instruction
He systematically broke all his oaths prior to the commencement of the Kurukṣetra war
He sought formal expiation through a rājasūya yajña before confronting Duḥśāsana
He allowed Yudhiṣṭhira to fulfill his vows on his behalf to preserve ritual purity
distractor_pool: He refused to fight until Kṛṣṇa absolved him of his previous declarations
He replaced martial retaliation with spiritual austerities in the forest
questions.answer: He remained open to abandoning his vows for peace during diplomatic consultations and struck Duryodhana upon Kṛṣṇa's tactical instruction
accepted_answers: He remained open to abandoning his vows for peace during diplomatic consultations and struck Duryodhana upon Kṛṣṇa's tactical instruction
questions.explanation: During the Udyoga Parva peace mission, Bhīma favored peace even if it meant foregoing his vows. Furthermore, his decisive action in the mace duel followed Kṛṣṇa's real-time guidance rather than blind vengeance.
questions.source_quote: Yet in Udyoga Parva, when Kṛṣṇa consulted all the Pāṇḍavas... Bhīma favoured peace, willing to forgo his vows... Bhīma tired and Kṛṣṇa signalled him to strike the thigh; so the thigh-blow followed Kṛṣṇa's instruction, not merely his vow.

questions.stem: Why does the author designate Śrī Kṛṣṇa, rather than Bhīṣma, as the true archetype of Pratijñā (The Vow)?
stem_variants: What defines Kṛṣṇa as the genuine archetype of Pratijñā compared to Bhīṣma's tragic archetype?
options: Kṛṣṇa treated vows dynamically as instruments of universal Dharma, refusing to let a personal pledge obstruct the destruction of adharma
Kṛṣṇa never made any verbal commitments, thereby remaining immune to ethical compromises
Kṛṣṇa strictly observed every minor austerity without changing his stance under any battle condition
Kṛṣṇa coerced both sides into adopting identical rules of engagement prior to the war
distractor_pool: Kṛṣṇa passed his vows onto Arjuna through the teachings of the Bhagavad Gītā
Kṛṣṇa's vows were sanctioned by the devas through celestial showers of flowers
questions.answer: Kṛṣṇa treated vows dynamically as instruments of universal Dharma, refusing to let a personal pledge obstruct the destruction of adharma
accepted_answers: Kṛṣṇa treated vows dynamically as instruments of universal Dharma, refusing to let a personal pledge obstruct the destruction of adharma
questions.explanation: While Bhīṣma was trapped and rendered helpless by his inflexible vow, Kṛṣṇa showed that an oath must yield to higher Dharma when necessary—demonstrated when he charged at Bhīṣma with a chariot wheel despite having pledged not to bear arms.
questions.source_quote: Kṛṣṇa was not held back by his vow and acted with clarity for Dharma: the true Pratijñā archetype, unlike Bhīṣma who trapped himself.
